editions.text:
The day added up to 374 feeder visits and 23 species, both above the past week's averages of 308.0 visits and 20.3 species, while detections came to 426, a little under the 442.7 average. Of the 23 species, 20 were heard and 13 seen, with 10 both heard and seen. Tufted Titmouse was the first visual of the day at 0 min after sunrise, and Northern Cardinal the last at 674 min after sunrise, 2 min after sunset.

All 14 species recorded on each of the past seven days were present again, including Mourning Dove, Eastern Phoebe with 72 detections, and Tufted Titmice with 113 seen visits. Eight species recorded earlier in the week were missing today: Red-shouldered Hawk, Brown-headed Cowbird, Cedar Waxwing, Yellow-bellied Sapsucker, Broad-winged Hawk, Eastern Meadowlark, Northern Flicker, and Rose-breasted Grosbeak. No species was a first confident visual record at this station, and none was heard for the first time.

The audio source was switched many times through the day, moving between the pi, pi-mic and c120 sources, so the heard counts draw on more than one microphone. No feeder change was logged for this day. The highlights were a Blue Jay perching on the birdbath rim to drink and bathe, and a single woodpecker foraging on the ground near the seed feeder cage.
